answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require hardware-rooted remote attestation. An agent executes inside a tamper-resistant enclave validated by a consensus kernel. Attackers incur the verifiable capital cost of acquiring physical silicon per identity, as factory-fused private keys prevent software emulation. However, microarchitectural side channels leave isolation on a fragile ledge, and high device costs strand lightweight agents in a computational tundra.
